headline: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg and Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang pushed back on calls to slow AI development, saying safety work will set the leading labs apart.
score_reason: Pool score kept: two senior Meta leaders enter a central industry debate; positions, not actions.
importance_line: Meta is one of the few companies with the money to build frontier AI, so its stance on pace and outside review matters to regulators and rival labs, but the claim that alignment pays commercially is Meta's own argument, and Meta delayed its Muse model for months for safety work.
summary: Stocktwits reports that Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive of Meta, and Alexandr Wang, Meta's AI chief, said on X that labs should keep advancing while building safeguards, with Zuckerberg writing "Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind" and both urging independent evaluators; Zuckerberg called spending most computing power on serving people, rather than racing toward AI that improves its own abilities, one of the best ways to keep AI safe. Their posts name no one but come amid a debate in which Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, has called for slowing frontier AI so safety can catch up, while President Donald Trump argues against slowing the US race with China.
notes: Reply-type story: posts answer 'calls to slow AI' without naming a person; context names Amodei as the main voice for slowing. Posting date not stated (article published 14 Oct).
